clue.text: See 4
Man dressed as Scotsman upset English just the same

indicators.note: the man is clothed in the garment, so his letters sit inside it
in a down clue upset turns the garment's letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: a kilt is the Scotsman's traditional dress
he stands for a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man dressed up as a Scot has annoyed the English all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns KILT over in this down clue, giving TLIK; 'dressed as' means the man wears it, so he goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'and the like' means things of a similar sort, much as 'just the same'.

clue.text: Amusing pockets to 9

definitions.note: the cross-reference points to the seat in 9 across alone

indicators.note: fun puts the next word in its pocket, holding it inside

parts.note: something amusing is fun
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something funny is tucked into a car seat.
explanation.definitionFit: This low Japanese-style mattress folds up into a sofa seat.

clue.text: King penguin?

parts.note: the question mark invites another royal penguin: a top-ranking monarch also names the biggest penguin species

explanation.definitionFit: A ruler above kings shares a name with the largest species of Antarctic penguin.

clue.text: Expensive entertaining revolting upper-class twit, promising to miss starter that's calorific

indicators.note: steep hosts the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: steep means expensive, as a steep price
icky means revolting or disgusting
a toff is a snobbish upper-class person

indicators.note: the opening letter of the promising word is dropped

parts.note: budding means promising, as a budding star

explanation.surface: A rich, disgusting upper-class idiot is being hosted, while a promising dish skips its first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' means the expensive word hosts the two guests inside; 'to miss starter' drops the first letter. A toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: This rich British dessert of date sponge drenched in toffee sauce is notoriously fattening.

clue.text: Try to catch hockey initially, or a bit of some cricket, perhaps?

definitions.text: a bit of some cricket, perhaps?

indicators.note: the try word grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to tax is to try, as in trying one's patience

indicators.note: only the first letter of hockey is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sporting question about whether hockey or cricket tests you more.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the insect, not the game: its middle body section is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's middle body segment, between head and abdomen, is one part of a cricket.

clue.text: Sardine this moronic, oddly fishy as a 16 down?

definitions.note: 16 down is a bloater, read here as something that bloats you

indicators.note: fishy means suspect or not right, so the letters are disordered
only the odd-placed letters of moronic are taken

explanation.surface: A dim-witted sardine seems suspicious when served as a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks MRNC from moronic; 'fishy' then shuffles all fifteen letters. 16 down's fish is read as something that bloats you.
explanation.definitionFit: The big festive meal leaves diners stuffed, a bloater in the sense of something that bloats.

clue.text: Wages rocketing, game not half barking!

indicators.note: in a down clue rocketing sends the letters upwards, reading back

parts.note: pay means wages

indicators.note: only the first half of the game's name is kept

parts.note: ping-pong is the game of table tennis

explanation.surface: Pay soars, but the games are not half crazy!
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocketing' sends PAY up the column as YAP; 'not half' keeps PING from PINGPONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that is barking is making shrill, noisy yelps.

clue.text: Two painters blended in red mark

indicators.note: the letters are mixed together like paints

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of artists mix colours together to produce a red smudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' rearranges TWO PAINTERS as PORTWINESTA; the 'in' then sits unchanged at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish-purple birthmark on the skin is named after the colour of a fortified wine.

clue.text: What's testable in a crash?

parts.note: crash-test dummies check how a car's safety restraint holds in a collision

explanation.definitionFit: Car safety restraints are tried out in crash tests to see if they hold the passenger.

clue.text: Old backward language of criminals in pubs, still

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the pair of pubs

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house, so two pubs give two of them

indicators.note: the slang word is read from end to start

parts.note: argot is the slang of thieves and the underworld

explanation.surface: Old thieves' slang, spoken backwards in bars, persists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns ARGOT into TOGRA; a 'still' is a single frame shot from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single static picture, a snapshot taken on film.

clue.text: See 6
Brown trapping Blair finally, Labour leader cut short in dispatch

indicators.note: the colour holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: only the last letter of Blair is taken
the final letter of the leader's name is cut off

parts.note: John Smith led the UK Labour Party before Tony Blair

explanation.surface: A political story of Gordon Brown hemming in Tony Blair, with a Labour leader dispatched early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes H from SMITH; John Smith led Britain's Labour Party in 1992-94, just before Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch a message is to send it out, as a radio does.

clue.text: Analyser put paper cups in wiggly line

indicators.note: the paper and cups go inside the jumbled line
a wiggly line is a bent one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper
a bra has cups

explanation.surface: Someone asked to put paper cups in a wavy row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiggly' rearranges the line as LEIN; the surface 'put' is just a link. The left side of the brain is popularly the analytical half.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain's left hemisphere is popularly held to handle logic and analysis.

clue.text: Professional calling, else fashioned in lies?

indicators.note: the remade letters go inside the lies word

parts.note: tales are lies, as in telling tales

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: A suggestion that cold-callers spin falsehoods for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges the word else as ELES; the question mark hints that phone sellers may tell fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling by phone is a trade built on making calls.

clue.text: Superior sticks around

indicators.note: the word is turned around to read backwards

parts.note: gums stick things, as glue

explanation.surface: A snooty person keeps hanging about.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling superior is being complacently self-satisfied.

clue.text: See 9
Fish left in hat

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the hat

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat

explanation.surface: A fish left inside someone's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a type of smoked, salted herring.

clue.text: Canal man hurried to tether boat, not heading back

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read from end to start
the hurried word ties the boat inside it

parts.note: sped means hurried

indicators.note: the first letter of the boat is lost

parts.note: a vessel is a boat

explanation.surface: A man of the canal rushes to moor his boat, bow pointing backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not heading' loses the boat's first letter; 'to tether' ties it inside; 'back' then reverses the lot, SPESSELED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand de Lesseps was the French diplomat who developed the Suez Canal.

clue.text: Ovum has to do well, roughly speaking?

indicators.note: the excel word, said loosely, approximates the answer's sound

parts.note: to excel is to do well

explanation.surface: An egg must succeed, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is the female reproductive cell, the egg.

clue.text: See 4
See 27
The Barbarian crossing street, little time for uniform

indicators.note: Conan straddles the street, holding it inside

parts.note: Conan the Barbarian is the fictional sword-wielding hero
T is the short form for time

explanation.surface: Conan the Barbarian crosses a road, short of time for his uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uniform is unchanging or steady throughout.

clue.text: Spurs getting to grips with new balls?

indicators.note: the spurs hold the next letter inside

parts.note: to spur is to goad, so spurs are goads

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspurs players grappling with new footballs.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; 'balls' here means testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for testicles is the reproductive glands, the male sex organs.

clue.text: Monsoon ending, doctor between two thunderclouds

indicators.note: only the last letter of monsoon is taken
the doctor sits between the two strokes

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor stands between two storm clouds as the monsoon ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain-bearing grey clouds of thunder are nimbus clouds, plural nimbi.

clue.text: Do it in dry surroundings — this dripping?

indicators.note: the dry word surrounds the action words

parts.note: stale bread is dry
act it means to perform it, so do it

explanation.surface: Something dripping in dry surroundings, as in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave formation hanging from the roof grows from limy water drips.

clue.text: Female cuckoo steals one

indicators.note: the mad word takes the one inside it

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for mad
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A female cuckoo is stealing an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl or young unmarried woman is a female.

clue.text: Again, arrange to see Blackpool, perhaps

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
sort means arrange

explanation.surface: A plan to arrange another visit to Blackpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is a seaside town in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackpool is an example of a seaside holiday town.

clue.text: Unknown craft not to be trusted breaking surface at sea

indicators.note: the dishonest word breaks into the jumbled letters
at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lying person is not to be trusted

explanation.surface: A mysterious ship emerges dishonestly at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the surface as FSAUCER; the dishonest word breaks in after its first letter. 'Unknown craft' points to a UFO.
explanation.definitionFit: A UFO is a craft of unknown origin, often pictured as a disc.
